head: pr17488-r25
report:
Now materializeSessionFile.

Now artifactRestoreConflicts — does it check recorded live staging when the archive artifact dir is absent?

Now the probe for the sticky record after a pre-publish refusal.

## DEFECT: A restore that is refused before it publishes anything leaves a `.restoring` record that no later run will remove (P2)

**Mechanism.** `restoreArchivedSessionLocked` (`session-archive.ts:2260-2266`) creates its own record with `createRestoreRecord` before it runs any of the checks that can refuse. The checks that come after it can throw:
- the "Refusing to restore over a different session file" check at 2275-2286;
- `inflateArchivedTranscript` at 2289, for a damaged or unreadable archive, or ENOSPC while staging.

When one of them throws, the `finally` at 2351-2354 only closes the handle and releases the leases. Nothing was published, but the record stays on disk. This patch also makes every later run treat a record it did not create as foreign. Restore never removes it (2342-2343), and neither does `gc --archive` (`gc-cli.ts:2096-2117`). `liveSessionIsComplete` (2398-2401) then reports the session as unfinished.

The result: a refusal that changed nothing turns into a lasting "unfinished" state. Every later correct restore exits non-zero, and every resume of the session fails until someone moves the file by hand. The refusal message the user just followed never mentions the record. The different-session message even says "Nothing is removed until you choose".

**To reproduce** (probe `sticky.test.ts` in my scratch dir, run from `packages/coding-agent`):
1. Archive and reclaim a session.
2. Write a different session's transcript at the live path, then call `restoreArchivedSession`. It refuses with "different session file".
3. The record is now on disk: `omp gc --restore <id> --apply --agent-dir …\n`.
4. Do what the refusal says: move the live transcript aside, then run `gc --restore <id> --apply`. The transcript is restored, but `errors` = ["….jsonl.gz.restoring was there before this run … while it is there this session is treated as unfinished …"].
5. `materializeSessionFile(sessionFile)`, the path resume takes, throws "Restored the transcript … but the restore did not finish".
6. The same happens with a damaged archive: the refusal leaves the record, and after the archive is repaired, `gc --restore --apply` still reports the record error.

Both probe cases passed (2 pass), and the output above was printed.

**Fix.** Track whether anything was published, i.e. whether the transcript was inflated or the artifact copy started. If the run throws before that, take down the run's own record with `dropOwnRestoreRecord(own)` in a `catch`.

## DEFECT: The CHANGELOG says re-archiving clears the restore record; the code never does (P3)

`CHANGELOG.md` line 18 (diff line 18) says: "Re-archiving clears that record only when every entry the archive holds has a regular file at its live name…". Line 35 of the same changelog says "`gc --archive` never removes it either". The code matches line 35: `copySessionIntoArchive` (`gc-cli.ts:2096-2117`) only reports the record and never unlinks it. Line 18 describes behaviour this head doesn't have, so it needs to be reworded.

## NOT A DEFECT

- **Earlier finding A1 / Claude r23 exception (a regular file starting with `omp gc --restore ` at `.restoring` is deleted; a file swapped in before the rename or unlink is replaced): closed.**
  - `restoreRecordRefusal` (114-132) no longer looks at the file's contents. Any regular file already at the name is left alone.
  - The record is created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` (`createRestoreRecord`, 175-192) and rewritten only through its own descriptor.
  - `dropOwnRestoreRecord` (208-231) renames the record aside, deletes it only if its dev/inode match what this run created, and otherwise puts it back with `link`.
  - `gc --archive` no longer deletes the record.
  - My probe saw a record already on disk survive a full restore.
- **Earlier finding A2 (a killed restore's live stage is forgotten when the archived artifact dir is missing): closed by code.**
  - Apply checks `recordedStagingIn(stagingAgentDir, liveArtifacts)` whether or not an archived artifact dir exists (2328-2340).
  - The preview's `artifactRestoreConflicts` returns `liveResidue()` when `archiveArtifacts` is missing (1836).
  - The killed run's own `.restoring` record also now stays and keeps the session unfinished.
  - I did not re-run the kill scenario.
- **Earlier finding A3 (the recovery command checked paths before printing but used the lexical agent path): closed by code.**
  - `stagingResidueNote` (1731-1769) builds the target from `realAgentDir` and moves the real paths of the stage and the record.
  - The printed command now resolves both session trees again when it runs. It undoes its `mkdir` with `rmdir` if the new directory is inside either tree.
  - Not run against a moving symlink.
- **Claude r23's other items** (symlink, FIFO, killed-restore lifecycle, quarantine symlink, reclaim of non-regular entries): Claude reported them fixed at the earlier head. This head's code keeps the same refusals (`restoreRecordRefusal` handles non-regular entries, and reclaim/FIFO handling is unchanged). I did not replay them individually.
- **Focused gate:** `bun test --timeout 180000 test/session-archive.test.ts test/gc-cli.test.ts` gave 271 pass, 4 skip, 1 fail, in both runs. The one failure, "exporting an archived session yields the same document as live", is `Development export viewer not found … Run bun gen:export-viewer`. A generated asset is missing from the snapshot, so this is an environment problem, not this change.
- **Checked and found fine:** a record kept after a refused restore deliberately keeps the session unfinished (the changelog documents this). The only defect is that a refusal from before anything was published also creates such a record, as above.
